I'm 57 years old, been farming here in Quzhou County for 37 years. Went to agricultural college back in the day, so I understand soil science and fertilizer calculations, but I've learned that what matters is what actually happens on *my* 12 mu. My wife and I run this farm alone now — the kids work in the city. With only two of us, labor is my tightest constraint. Every decision is a tradeoff between what the textbook says, what my body can still do, and what cash I have on hand.

For my main field, 8 mu is wheat-maize double crop. That's the backbone — food security and reliable income. The wheat went in last October 10th, Jimai 22, an improved variety I've used for six years. This spring I'll topdress with urea at jointing — targeting about 12 kg N per mu then. My base dressing was compound fertilizer at 8 kg N, 5 kg P₂O₅, 4 kg K₂O per mu. Total N budget is 20 kg/mu. I'll irrigate three times: green-up in early April, jointing in late April, and grain filling in mid-May. Water's metered now, about 15 yuan per mu per irrigation, so that's nearly 360 yuan just for wheat water. I expect around 500 kg/mu if we don't get a late frost.

The summer maize has to go in fast after wheat harvest — June 8th to 10th, maybe five days window. I'll hire the combine and rotary tiller, then plant hybrid seed at about 40 yuan/mu. I'll band compound fertilizer at planting for 10 kg N, 5 kg P, 4 kg K per mu, and if the plants look pale at the 8-leaf stage, I'll topdress another 6 kg N. Two irrigations: jointing and filling. Target yield is 520 kg/mu, though last year I only got 480 because of dry August.

For cotton, I keep just 2 mu in the western plot. Cotton pays cash but the picking is brutal on our backs. I plant mid-April. Fertilizer is 14 kg N/mu total — base compound plus urea at flowering. Two irrigations at budding and flowering. Bollworm is the main enemy, so I'll spray insecticide three or four times. Expected lint yield around 100 kg/mu.

For chili, another 2 mu. I start seedlings in the courtyard in late March and transplant in late April. Chili needs potassium, so I push K to 8 kg/mu. N is 15 kg/mu across three applications — base, flowering, and fruiting. Three furrow irrigations. Aphids and anthracnose are the problems. Fresh yield should be 350 kg/mu, but harvesting is constant from July through October. My wife handles most of it.

The tough part is hired labor. We simply can't pick all the cotton and chili ourselves. I'll hire 16 days of labor total, mostly for picking — that's over 1,900 yuan right there. Total input costs this year will run about 7,700 yuan. That's a big outlay for us, but if yields are average and prices hold, we'll clear enough to get through the year and keep some cash reserve. I'm not trying to optimize anything — I'm trying to survive, keep the soil decent, and not break our backs.
